summary: Comsky Books is a local-first, keyboard-first TallyPrime-parity accounting app (web + Electron) with a cloud sync backend. After Phase 29 (parity wave 3, built 2026-10-22; three of its five clusters, cancel and party terms, e-way and dispatch, and export and share, were also adversarially reviewed and fixed; committed 2cee555 and deployed 2026-10-23 (BETA; authenticated cloud flows not exercised on the VM); the deployed tree is 687c062, which only adds doc edits) it covers 250 of 381 audited TallyPrime features and is partial on 58 (about 73% weighted, 73.2 before rounding; the 73 still missing include no P0). It was 258 / 44 / 79 (73.5%) after Phase 24. Wave 3 moved 15 rows: six up (cancelled-register to covered; credit-limit-override, eway-bill, eway-register, report-email and numbering-override-multiuser from missing to partial) and nine DOWN from covered to partial, because building this wave showed those rows had been scored on a first slice (credit-limit, interest-simple, interest-bills, interest-report, price-levels, report-export, export-pdf, import-excel and deleted-tracking: each row now says what TallyPrime still does that it does not). The weighted figure falls from 73.5 to 73.2 for that reason; the product did not get worse. The rule was the board's own: a row this wave touched is judged against all of Tally's behaviour, covered only when the builder AND the review pass agree, and anything not compared with a live TallyPrime, the GST portal or the IRP says so in its row. The other corrections proposed in docs/research/tally-parity-recheck-2026-10.md (its section d1) are NOT applied: they await the owner, and section (h) of that file lists what wave 3 addressed. Wave 3 also built things that have no row among the 381 and so move no count: dispatch, consignee and transport details on the voucher, bulk invoice print, a static UPI QR on the invoice, and share by WhatsApp and e-mail link (the nearest rows, eway-bill, eway-register, report-email and tax-invoice-print, carry them in their notes). Phase 24 moved 56 rows to a new status and rewrote the note on 48 more, in two waves: GST identity and dated rate history, GSTR-1/3B/9 and portal JSON, reverse charge / ITC reversal / advances / adjustment journals, the TDS/TCS engine (cumulative register, certificates, challan reconciliation, interest), bank-statement import and cheque suite, report platform (F12, percentages, columns, basis, explode, saved views), operator security and company passcode, print configuration, backup scheduling and Data Check, costing methods, company split, e-invoice records and sync mismatch detection. Six P0 rows are partial after Phase 29: mfg-stock-posting, gst-json-export, report-f12-config, company-vault, import-xml and, new in wave 3, report-export (JSON, XML, HTML and image export are not built, and a PDF needs the desktop app to be written without a dialog; Excel and CSV are built). Largest remaining blocks: job work and multi-BOM manufacturing, multi-currency, payroll income tax and salary revisions, voucher class, eTDS/FVU and 27Q. Everything that has not been compared with a live TallyPrime, the GST portal or the IRP says so in its row. Capabilities Tally does not have are listed under 'beyond' and are never counted in the percentage. Phase 26 (the Zoho-style UX wave: menu v2, quick-create, the navigation stack, row filters, shared views, the Reports Center) moved no parity row: it is 'beyond' work. Its two nearest rows, report-range-filter and report-value-filter, stay partial because the filter is on five report screens (Day Book, voucher registers, Ledger Vouchers, Receivables, Payables), not the main statements; their notes now say what was built. Phase 27 (the Settings window and configurable shortcuts, wave B) moved no parity row either: it is 'beyond' work (rows b-settings and b-shortcuts). Phase 28 (Dashboard v2: a period-aware board of 22 widgets with charts, as-at figures and drill-through) moved no parity row either: it is 'beyond' work (row b-dashboard-v2). Both were committed together as 5c94342 and their web app was deployed to the VM on 2026-10-21 (BETA: built, reviewed, never used by a customer); the backend half of Phase 27 (backend/src/conflict.js, sync.js) was deployed on 2026-10-23 together with Phase 29's backend (the VM ran the a0fffd6 backend code until then; the rule has not been exercised on the VM). Phase 30 (custom fields v2, reporting by field, stock by field and the mouse Back control; built and reviewed 2026-10-24, merged into main as 1d22e84 on 2026-10-25, NOT DEPLOYED) moved no parity row either: it is 'beyond' work (rows b-custom-fields, b-entry-rules, b-field-reports, b-stock-variants and b-back-control, all marked built, not deployed), and a no-code custom field is not TallyPrime's TDL, so tdl-customization stays missing; the counts stay 250 / 58 / 73. The batch, serial/IMEI, scanning and label engines merged as 5aee765 are pure code wired to no screen and have no row.

features.name: Credit limit (amount) per party with enforcement

One engine (core/creditLimit.ts) serves the voucher, Bulk Entry and the Credit Limits report: a customer's limit measures what they owe (Dr), a supplier's (under Sundry Creditors) what we owe them (Cr); the figure is the balance on the voucher's date plus what the voucher adds; an altered voucher is re-counted and asked again only when its figure rises; a limit reached exactly is not over. Over the limit is a warning that can be overridden, and the override needs a reason, kept on the voucher (creditOverride). Partial against Tally: the override is a reason recorded by whoever enters the voucher, not an authorisation by another user and not Tally's documented override by post-dated transactions; no group-wise limit grid (Alter > Credit Limits); no blocking mode. features.name: Auto (manual override) & multi-user auto numbering
features.tally: Override auto number inline; multi-user dup prevention.
features.ours: Cloud numbering. On Accept a signed-in, online device asks the server for the voucher's number (POST /sync/next-number v2: one request per draft, keyed to the voucher id, never below the device's own next number; series = company x type x restart window; prefix, suffix, zero pad and the {fy}/{mm} tokens stay on the device). If the cloud cannot answer, the voucher keeps its local number saved PROVISIONAL (a persisted flag plus a worklist) and each sync claims those numbers first; a clash is flagged, recorded in the Sync Mismatch Report through the duplicate-number path and NEVER renumbered silently (Renumber asks first with No armed, takes a fresh cloud number and writes an audit note; it changes the voucher number only, not its New Ref bill). The voucher screen, Bulk Entry, the Stock Journal, payroll and attendance vouchers and salary disbursement take part (a collision on the last four is flagged, not prevented); RCM and Rule 37 journals and bank-statement import still number from the local count. Manual-numbering types and a signed-out app are exactly as before. Partial: Tally's Auto (manual override) numbering and multiple named series are not built, and the BACKEND HALF WAS DEPLOYED 2026-10-23 (backend/sql/008_voucher_series.sql applied by npm run migrate, backend/src/numbering.js, sync.js; the three number routes answer 401 without a token on the live host). Proven on simulated devices and on a real Postgres 17, never with two real devices on the VM; no signed-in call has run on the VM's Fastify route wrapper (no test account was created on the live host). Phase 29: built (no separate review pass was reported for this cluster), deployed 2026-10-23 (BETA; authenticated cloud flows not exercised on the VM).

features.name: Simple interest calculation on ledgers
features.tally: Activate interest, rate/period/basis per ledger; report.
features.ours: The party ledger form has Interest rate (% a year, 0 to 100; blank or 0 is none) and Interest style (365-day year by default, or the 30-day month, a 360-day year) as tail fields. The Interest Calculation report (core/interestCalc.ts) was rewritten in this wave: as committed it charged the CLOSING balance for the WHOLE period (17,950.68 on 1,00,000 at 18% for an invoice raised the day before the period ended, about 99 by the daily balance) and added interest on a balance we owe into the same total as interest owed to us. A ledger that is not bill-wise is now charged on its DAILY BALANCE (the balance standing at the end of each day, first and last day counted), interest receivable and payable are two columns never added together, and interest stops at today (a period that starts after today shows none). Partial: no F11 switch to activate interest, no bank-date basis, no compound or per-voucher override, the rate and style are on party ledgers only (not bank or OD ledgers), and the arithmetic was not compared with a live TallyPrime. Phase 29: built and reviewed, deployed 2026-10-23 (BETA; authenticated cloud flows not exercised on the VM).

features.name: Company GST registration setup
features.tally: Reg type, GSTIN, state, periodicity, e-inv/eway applicability.
features.ours: GSTIN is checked for structure and the GSTN mod-36 check character (core/gstin.ts). An invalid new GSTIN or an unlisted state asks 'Save anyway?' with the exact reason (a caution, not a refusal); an old invalid GSTIN never blocks an unrelated edit; a valid GSTIN fills a blank State and PAN. features.name: Party GST details (reg type, party type)

One supplyKind() rule classifies B2B/B2C/export/SEZ/deemed export for GSTR-1, 3B and 9; untyped legacy parties classify as before. A supply to or by an SEZ, or to an overseas party, is always inter-state (IGST even when the SEZ sits in the company's own state). Contradictory type/GSTIN/state blocks the save. Tally import maps GSTREGISTRATIONTYPE. Limit: SEZ and Deemed Export are never inferred from a Tally file and do not round-trip as a distinct type.

Saving a changed rate or HSN asks 'Applicable from' and appends to a history; Alt+H opens the dated grid. A pure resolver (core/gstRates.ts) answers line override, item, group chain, ledger, company, in the company's chosen order (researched against TallyPrime help, cited in code). The voucher line prefills for the voucher date, shows its source and takes a per-line override (Alt+H) that wins everywhere; saved invoices keep their own snapshot. Not built: GST Classification tier, accounting-group tier, 'apply to all items'. Default order (stock item first) is Tally's second documented option, kept so existing item invoices do not change; Tally's documented default is ledger first (owner decision pending).

Phase 29: the Ship-to block prints the voucher's consignee (Deliver-to on inward documents), the e-way bill number and the portal's valid-till date print when held, an owner-chosen static UPI QR can print (sales invoice with the bank block, a valid UPI ID, switched on, default off), bulk print builds one job from a register selection using each voucher's own paper, copies and labels (more than 100 is refused whole), and a cancelled voucher never prints.

features.tally: Registered outward grouped by GSTIN, rate-wise.

The portal's own change lagged the law (GSTN advisory of 3 Sep 2024); the app follows the law.

Export credit notes go to CDNUR as EXPWP/EXPWOP; exports plus SEZ equal GSTR-3B 3.1(b) (asserted). Limit: rt for WOPAY rows is the posted rate (0); whether the portal wants 0 or the goods' rate is unconfirmed (SCHEMA? in code).

Those amounts leave B2B/B2CL/B2CS through one shared splitter (core/gstNil.ts) that GSTR-3B and GSTR-9 also use, and which reads a ledger's own taxability. Table 8 equals 3B 3.1(c)+(e) (asserted); exports and SEZ supplies stay zero-rated as whole documents.

RCM, imports 6E/6F), Part IV (9 tax paid). Portal-shaped. Not built: Tables 8 and 10-14 (amendments, ISD, transitional credit); Table 7 reversals are one line.

features.ours: GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B JSON come from pure core builders (gstr1.ts, gstr3b.ts) shared with the screens and the reconciliation: 2-digit state codes, rchrg, inv_typ, exp, nil, rate-wise HSN with cess, doc_issue, at/txpd, B2CS by pos+rate; 3B adds itc_avl by type, itc_rev, itc_net, itc_inelg, inward_sup and coded 3.2. features.name: e-Invoice IRN generation + signed QR
features.tally: IRP JSON, IRN/ack/QR, print QR, cancel.
features.ours: IRNs are never generated here. Registered IRNs, Ack, signed QR and e-way numbers are recorded per invoice (einvoices table, Dexie v8) by importing the portal's results and printed with a scannable QR; an INV-01 v1.1 payload is built, validated and exported for upload on the customer's own portal login. The old made-up IRN exists only in the sample company, reads MOCK - NOT A VALID IRN on screen, print and Edit Log, and is removable; a synced 'portal' row is believed only if its IRN is the hash of its own invoice. Party city/PIN, company city and a Service item flag are tail fields; IRP document-number rules are cautioned at Accept. Not built: any IRP/GSP call (needs TLS, a credential vault, a partner contract), cancel, e-way by IRN, GSTIN lookup. Signed-QR signatures are not verified, so a hash-consistent forgery would pass. Phase 29: the INV-01 builder now writes DispDtls, ShipDtls and EwbDtls from the voucher's Alt+S details (88 assertions; a change to the ship-to or dispatch-from address of a registered invoice is asked about on alteration), and cancelling a voucher that carries an IRN warns to cancel on the portal within 24 hours or raise a credit note; there is still no cancel API.

features.name: e-Invoice bulk generation / status / cancel
features.tally: Bulk IRN, status report, cancel window.
features.ours: B exports every pending invoice as portal upload JSON (checked first, split under 2 MB, one array per file); I imports the portal's results file in one step (preview, then Enter; rows it cannot match are refused). Not built: bulk generation through an API, status polling, cancel. The bulk-upload wrapper and the results-file layout are unverified (no real file).

features.name: e-Way Bill generation (JSON/API, Part A/B)
features.ours: Offline: no credentials and no API call. An opt-in Alt+S sub-panel on sales, purchase, credit-note, debit-note, delivery-note and receipt-note vouchers captures Part A and Part B (transporter, vehicle, distance, mode, transaction type) beside the dispatch and consignee details; it is not in the Enter walk, and a voucher that never opens it saves no key. core/ewb.ts validates against the rules it could cite (Rule 138(1) Rs 50,000 and the exempt-goods case, validity per 200 km or 20 km for over-dimensional cargo, the NIC EwbDtls tables and transport checks); every rule that rests on a secondary source is a caution, never an error, and is listed in EWB_UNCERTAIN (8 rules). It writes the portal's bulk-generation file ({ version, billLists }, about 500 bills a file) and imports the portal's results tolerantly (JSON or CSV, any key spelling, 12 or 24-hour clocks, spreadsheet damage such as 3.51E+11 flagged): a row attaches only when it names exactly one voucher and agrees on date, type, sender, receiver and value; one bill belongs to one document; a re-import is skipped; cancellation and extension are recognised. No e-way bill number is ever made up; the invoice prints the number and the portal's own valid-till date. A consignee in another state never moves the place of supply or the tax (IGST Act s.10(1)(b)), asserted byte for byte on GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B. Partial: nothing was ever uploaded to the portal (the bulk file's key names and version tag come from ERPNext's generator and a Vayana sample, SCHEMA?; the portal's own documents answered 403); no live generation, cancel, extend, Part B update or consolidated bill through an API (that needs a GSP, TLS and a credential vault); no QR on the invoice (its payload is undocumented); the ship-to GSTIN has no known bulk-file key; a State's own intra-State limit is unknown; the Tally XML export does not carry the consignee. Phase 29: built and reviewed, deployed 2026-10-23 (BETA; authenticated cloud flows not exercised on the VM).

features.name: e-Way Bill report / register
features.ours: The e-Way Bills register (Gateway > GST, key W; Go To; the palette; the Reports Center; no left-rail row) shows each bill as needs details (Alt+S), ready, generated, expiring within 8 hours, expired, cancelled, changed after the bill, or not in the books while the bill is still alive; X marks one cancelled; a live bill blocks deleting its voucher; the audit log names an e-way row as such. Partial: its data arrives only by importing the portal's results file (layout unverified, no real file, no status polling), and every purchase over Rs 50,000 reads Details needed even when the supplier will generate the bill. Phase 29: built and reviewed, deployed 2026-10-23 (BETA; authenticated cloud flows not exercised on the VM).

features.name: Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM)
features.ours: Reverse-charge purchases are read by one shared engine (core/rcm.ts) in GSTR-3B 3.1(d)/4(A)(2)-(3), GSTR-9 and the Ineligible ITC report. A Reverse Charge Register shows each with its status and posts a linked Journal (Dr input credit / Cr output liability) on P/A, or on save when Company > GST Setup is Automatic; the return reads the posted legs and flags orphan, out-of-date or duplicate Journals; Mark Optional carries the Journal with the purchase. Not built: self-invoice print; liability falls on the voucher/Journal date, not the statutory time of supply. With Manual posting, a purchase flipped to Optional on the voucher screen leaves its Journal live (the return skips it and warns).

features.name: Ineligible ITC / blocked credit (17(5))
features.ours: Ineligible ITC (17(5)) report: eligible vs blocked ITC per Purchase/DebitNote (Ledger.itcBlocked, item and extra-charge ledgers scanned), 3B 4(A) vs 4(D) split, and it now also lists blocked reverse-charge credit. Reversals and re-claims (Rule 37 and Journals) live on the ITC Reversal report.

features.name: ITC reversal / re-claim (42/43, 180-day)
features.ours: A GST-flagged Journal routes ITC reversals to 3B 4(B)(1) (rules 38/42/43) or 4(B)(2) (others) and re-claims to 4(A)(5). A Rule 37 report finds purchases unpaid 180 days from bill-wise outstanding, posts the reversal and the re-claim on payment as linked Journals (post-all asks first and is one undo step; U removes the current period's Journals only). Not built: Rule 42/43 common-credit ratio (amounts entered by hand), s.50 interest, Rule 37A, 4(D)(2) and ISD; Rule 37 needs bill-wise suppliers.

features.name: GST tax liability on advance receipts
features.tally: Advance receipt raises GST liability; adjust on invoice.
features.ours: The GST rate of an advance receipt is set on its 11A row (R) and stored on the receipt's Advance allocation; tax is worked inside the amount received (CGST/SGST intra-state, IGST inter-state). 11A/11B follow FIFO per period, GSTR-1 exports at/txpd, GSTR-3B 3.1(a) and tax payable carry the net (11A less 11B), GSTR-9 shows 4F and the recon shows it as a reconciling line. Not posted to ledgers, by design; services only.

features.name: GST composition handling (CMP-08)
features.ours: Reg type selectable but no composition logic.

features.name: Bill of Supply print format
features.ours: Bill of Supply report: lists zero-tax/exempt/nil/non-GST sales; Enter opens a tax-column-free print layout titled BILL OF SUPPLY with the composition declaration gated on gstRegType.

features.name: GST classifications / rate-setup master
features.ours: No GST classification master: it needs a new Dexie table and screens. Stock Group dated details are inherited by every item without its own, so one dated edit updates a whole group, but groups cannot share one classification. The resolver is layered so a classification tier can slot in.

features.name: Round-off ledger in GST invoice
features.tally: Auto round-off ledger to nearest rupee.
features.ours: Auto round-off: rounds the party receivable/payable to a whole rupee on GST accounting invoices, posts the diff to a Round Off ledger (after TDS/TCS).

features.name: GST transaction validation / exception resolution
features.ours: GST Validation buckets outward/inward vouchers Included/Uncertain/Excluded with reasons and drill to the voucher: invalid company or party GSTIN (structure and check character), missing GSTIN/HSN/rate, GSTIN state differing from the party state, contradictory party details, tax charged by a Composition supplier, export or SEZ supply without IGST and no LUT, e-invoice date passed with no IRN. A local cash/B2C sale with no state counts as local, as GSTR-1 reads it.

features.name: UQC mapping for HSN/returns
features.tally: Maps units to government UQC codes.
features.ours: Unit.uqc (GST unit code); HSN summary prefers UQC over the raw symbol for returns.

features.name: GSTR-3B vs 1 vs books reconciliation
features.ours: GST Reconciliation screen: Books vs GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B(3.1) per tax head with Difference column; RCM 3.1(d) annotated separately; books-only cess flagged (returns carry no cess). Shared voucherGstSummary basis.

features.name: Multi-GSTIN / branch return segregation
features.ours: Single GSTIN per company.

features.name: TDS activation (F11 with TAN/deductor)
features.tally: Enable TDS with TAN, deductor type.
features.ours: feats.tds gates assist/fields; no TAN/deductor capture.

features.name: Deductor statutory details (TAN, responsible person)
features.tally: TAN, deductor type, responsible person for returns.
features.ours: No TAN/deductor fields.

features.name: Nature of Payment master (section/rate/threshold)
features.tally: Section, with/without-PAN rates, individual vs company, dated.
features.ours: A nature carries dated terms (effective-from rows): rate for Individual/HUF, a company rate and, for sections like 194D, a third rate for a person other than a company; an explicit or s.206AA without-PAN rate; per-payment, per-year and per-month limits, each row with a source note. A voucher is taxed on the terms in force on its own date; a rate-history panel adds dated rows; a 'Verify with your CA' note stands on the master. Legacy flat natures compute exactly as before. Not added: 26Q section codes (file-format values unverified; the Income-tax Act 2025 renumbers sections from 1 Apr 2026).

features.name: Pre-seeded statutory natures (194C/J/I/H/A)
features.ours: 20 seeded natures (194C, 194J(a)/(b), 194I(a)/(b), 194IA, 194IB, 194H, 194M, 194A, 193, 194, 194D, 194G, 194O, 194Q, 194R, 194S, 194T, 195) with dated history (Finance (No.2) Act 2024 rate cuts, Finance Act 2025 limits), each term with a source note. A once-only migration (Company.tdsSeedVersion) adds them to existing companies, never re-adds a deleted seed, leaves edited natures alone and writes with no user stamp (not undoable). Not confirmed: FY 2026-27 changes; 194N is not seeded; the 195 rate is a placeholder.

features.name: Deductee type master & classification
features.tally: Deductee type drives rate and return classification.
features.ours: 11 deductee types (the original 5 plus Co-operative Society, Local Authority, Government and three Non-Resident types) select the rate class; the master shows which. A party with no type gets a visible 'TDS will NOT be deducted' warning at Accept; a non-resident gets a 'check s.195' note.

features.name: TDS expense/party ledger configuration
features.tally: Expense flagged TDS-applicable; party as deductee.
features.ours: tdsNatureId on expense; tdsDeductee on party; TDS ledger taxType=TDS.

features.name: TDS duty ledger (auto, under Duties & Taxes)
features.tally: TDS payable ledger typed to TDS with rounding.
features.ours: The voucher auto-creates a 'TDS - <section>' ledger under Duties & Taxes (taxType TDS + nature), one per nature so two natures sharing a section never share a ledger; computeTds rounds to the nearest rupee (s.288B).

features.name: Threshold & cumulative annual limit handling
features.tally: Single-bill AND cumulative annual limit before deducting.
features.ours: A pure register of each deductee's payments and TDS per nature and tax year decides what is due: single, annual, per-month and 'above the limit' (194Q) rules are measured on the year's total, a crossing deducts on the whole aggregate including the catch-up (194C-style natures), and what was already deducted is netted off (25,000 a month to one vendor deducts from month 3). The prompt shows the year to date, the catch-up and any earlier shortfall; Exceptions, 26Q, 16A and Deductee-wise read the same register and basis. Lines on an Any ledger are tagged at save, older vouchers stay a floor; payments made before the books began are not in it.

features.name: TDS on advance payments (deduct then adjust)
features.tally: Deduct on advance, reverse when bill booked.
features.ours: A Payment that debits a bill-wise party with an Advance reference prompts for TDS when the party has a default nature (Alt+E on the party ledger); the bill that later settles it (Agst Ref) deducts only on the balance, so advance then bill never double-deducts. One advance party per Payment (others are warned about); a Payment settling a bill never deducts.

features.name: Rate without PAN (higher 20%)
features.ours: s.206AA higher rate (20%, or the nature's rate if higher) applies when the PAN is blank, malformed or a placeholder (PANNOTAVBL, PANAPPLIED, PANINVALID), through one hasValidPan() test shared by the TDS plan, the nature picker, TCS 206CC, Exceptions, 26Q and the TCS report. The prompt reads 'no valid PAN, higher rate' and can be overridden.

features.name: PAN capture & format validation
features.ours: Ledger.pan is captured with a format check (core/gstin.ts); a valid GSTIN fills a blank PAN (GSTIN characters 3-12 are the PAN); placeholder values are recognised and treated as no PAN for withholding.

features.name: Lower/nil deduction certificate (197)
features.tally: Certificate no., lower rate, validity, limit.
features.ours: A party ledger can hold s.197 certificates (nature, number, rate, validity, limit of payments covered) in the Alt+E panel. Payments inside the validity bear the certificate rate up to its limit and the normal rate above; rate 0 is a nil certificate; an expired date reverts, another nature's certificate is ignored, and without a valid PAN it is ignored and said so. The prompt names the certificate and what the voucher would deduct without it; Form 16A carries the remark.

features.name: Surcharge & Health-Education Cess on TDS
features.ours: TdsNature.surchargePct + cessPct; computeTds/computeTcs apply surcharge on tax then cess on tax+surcharge (8 engine assertions).

features.name: TDS on GST-exclusive value
features.tally: Computes TDS excluding GST where prescribed.
features.ours: TDS is deducted on the expense lines' value without GST: itemsTotal on a purchase item invoice, the expense Dr row on an accounting voucher (GST sits on its own rows), as CBDT Circular 23/2017 treats GST shown separately (core/tds.ts tdsNatureBases, core/tdsRegister.ts). Not built: an opt-in to include GST when the supplier invoice does not show it separately.

features.name: Manual override of computed TDS
features.ours: Assist prompt is an editable amount field (TaxPrompt): Enter applies the possibly-edited figure, Esc skips deduction.

features.name: TDS deduction reversal / cancellation
features.ours: No reversal; manual journal needed.

features.name: TDS challan payment voucher (BSR/challan/date)
features.tally: Payment to govt with BSR, challan no/date, section breakup.
features.ours: A TDS deposit Payment (Dr on the TDS ledger) carries challan details (Alt+Y: BSR, serial, date deposited, interest and late fee included). The challan reconciliation applies each deposit FIFO to the oldest unpaid deduction of the same section (b/f first; 30-day sections on their own due date), holds an over-deposit as an advance, and lists deductions no deposit has reached. No NSDL/FVU file is produced.

features.name: Challan reconciliation (link deductions to challans)
features.tally: Reconcile deducted vs paid per section/month.
features.ours: Each deposit is applied FIFO per section to the oldest unpaid deduction, b/f first, using each section's own due date (30 days for 194-IA/IB/194M). The same month rows feed Challans & 26Q and the Quarterly tracker. No NSDL/FVU file is produced, by design.

features.name: TDS outstanding / payables report
features.ours: TDS report: nature summary + ledger vouchers drill, with Opening (b/f) from the TDS ledger's opening balance and pre-period postings.

features.name: Deductee-wise / party-wise TDS report
features.tally: TDS by deductee: paid, deducted, deposited.
features.ours: Deductee (party)-wise TDS: per party x nature with PAN, deductee type, section, rate, amount paid, TDS deducted; drills to ledger vouchers.

features.name: Form 26Q (resident non-salary eTDS return)
features.ours: TDS Challans & Returns builds the 26Q view from the books: deductee, PAN, section, amount paid (read from the voucher's expense lines, not back-computed from the rate), the rate actually deducted (rows differing from the rate in force are flagged, unattributable ones marked estimated), TDS and the challan allocation; exports an annexure CSV. Not built: FVU file, 26Q file-format section codes, 27Q.

features.ours: None.

features.ours: None.

features.ours: None.

features.name: Form 16A / TDS certificate

features.name: Form 27A (return cover sheet)
features.ours: None.

features.name: TDS uncertain transactions / exceptions
features.ours: TDS Exceptions report: Included/Uncertain/Excluded buckets (no valid PAN, deductee unset, per-nature below-threshold, expense-without-TDS-entry, declarations and certificates with the reason they apply or do not), postsToLedgers- guarded, drill to voucher; an earlier payment clears once the catch-up was deducted.

features.name: Quarterly period & due-date tracking
features.tally: Organizes by return quarter with due dates.
features.ours: TDS Quarterly tracker: FY quarters with 26Q due dates + status chips, deducted/deposited/payable, a B/F row, and a monthly deposit-due list (FIFO deposit-to-liability-month allocation; April challans clear March; 30-day sections on their own rows).

features.name: Interest / late-fee (234E, 201)
features.ours: TDS Interest & Late Fee screen: s.201(1A) interest (1.5% a month late deposit, 1% a month late deduction, part-month = full month, calendar months counted inclusively as TRACES does) and the s.234E fee (200 a day, capped at the quarter's tax, filing date typed per quarter), as labelled estimates, never posted. Deposit due dates follow the section (30 days for 194-IA/IB/194M). Not modelled: 194S for a specified person, a Government deductor, CBDT-extended dates, 234E on 26QB/QC/QD, the Income-tax Act 2025 renumbering.

features.name: TCS activation & collector config
features.ours: TCS enabled via F11 (features.tcs); TCS-payable ledger auto-created (taxType TCS) on first collection.

features.ours: TCS Nature of Goods master (206C) — name/section/rate/threshold, stored in tdsNatures with kind:TCS; 5 seeded (206C(1H)/scrap/minerals/timber/vehicle).

features.name: TCS collectee/buyer classification & PAN
features.ours: TCS runs on the same per-buyer register as TDS: 206C(1H) taxes only the part above the limit; a buyer with no PAN bears 1% on 206C(1H) and the higher of 5% or twice the rate on other 206C natures, in the voucher and the tracker alike. The buyer's company/non-company type reuses the ledger's deductee type (a tail field when TDS is off). 206C(1H) is treated as omitted from 1 Apr 2025 (rests on Tally's help page and secondary sources; the Act's text was not opened).

features.name: Automatic TCS collection on sales
features.ours: Auto TCS assist on Sales: sales/item ledger tcsNatureId triggers collection on invoice value; increases buyer Dr + posts TCS Cr; overridable amount.

features.name: TCS on receipt / 206C(1H) turnover threshold
features.tally: TCS above cumulative turnover per buyer.
features.ours: TCS 206C(1H) tracker on the shared per-buyer register: per-customer FY sale consideration, Rs 50 lakh limit crossing, 0.1% (1% no-PAN) on the excess only; collectible-TCS total. Shown as historical from 1 Apr 2025 (omission unconfirmed against the Act's text).

features.name: TCS challan payment & reconciliation
features.ours: TCS Outstanding report: nature-wise collected/paid/payable + TCS ledger vouchers; paid via normal payment voucher (Dr TCS ledger).

features.ours: None.

features.name: TDS/TCS opening balances (b/f unpaid)
features.ours: TDS and TCS summaries and reports show Opening (b/f): the TDS/TCS ledger's opening balance plus every posting before the period, so an April challan for March's tax pays against it instead of reading as a negative payable. The quarterly tracker shows a B/F row and the challan reconciliation seeds it as the first FIFO bucket (its deduction date is assumed, and said so).

features.name: Transporter/specific exemptions (declaration)
features.tally: No deduction for transporters with PAN (194C).
features.ours: A party ledger can carry a 194C(6) transporter declaration or a Form 15G/15H declaration for a named financial year (Alt+E panel). With a valid PAN, TDS is 0 on 194C (transporter) or on 192A/193/194/194A/194D/194DA/194EE/194K (15G/15H, resident Individual/HUF); the prompt says why, Exceptions lists the voucher as Excluded with the reason; without a PAN or outside the year the declaration does not count. The 15G/15H section list is conservative (rent left out: sources disagree).

features.name: Multi-nature single expense ledger
features.ours: An expense ledger can be 'Any (choose at entry)': the voucher asks for the nature before the TDS prompt (Esc = no TDS on that line). A voucher with several natures gets one prompt each ('1 of 2'), Alt+E changes a prompt's nature, and each nature posts to its own TDS ledger (two natures sharing a section no longer share a ledger). Bulk Entry warns for Any-ledgers (it never deducts).

features.name: Rounding of TDS amount (nearest rupee)
features.ours: computeTds/computeTcs round to the nearest rupee per s.288B (Math.round); TDS assist guarded so the party credit is never driven negative.

features.name: F12 Configure (per-report configuration)
features.tally: Dozens of context options per report.
features.ours: F12 lists only the options a report honours, plus that report's own, all remembered in 'tw-report-config-v1'; a chip and a lit F12 key show whenever anything is set. It is on Trial Balance, Group Summary, Balance Sheet, P&L, Day Book and Ledger Vouchers (narration, one Dr/Cr column, running balance), Stock Summary, the voucher registers and Bills Receivable/Payable, and the earlier adopters. features.name: Ctrl-B Change basis of values
features.ours: Ctrl+B (Alt+B where the browser keeps Ctrl+B) on Trial Balance and Group Summary opens Basis of Values: Closing Balance, Opening Balance, Debit/Credit Transactions or Net Transactions. The sub line and headings name the basis; it carries into drilled Group Summaries and works on comparative and change columns. Opening + Dr - Cr = Closing is asserted for every ledger on the sample books. Multi-year companies: closingBalances has no financial-year roll-over, so an Income/Expense ledger's opening on that basis includes earlier years' P&L.

features.name: Ctrl-F Auto Column (comparative multi-period)
features.ours: Single period column; no columnar engine.

features.name: New/Alter/Delete column (Alt+C/A/D)
features.ours: Trial Balance, Group Summary, Balance Sheet, P&L and Stock Summary share the column keys: C/Alt+C adds an as-on, period or Auto column (monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, yearly, aligned to the financial year), Alt+A alters, Alt+D deletes, R removes the last; columns are remembered per company and report; F12 adds Change columns (amount, or amount and %). Partial: no manual columns on Ratio Analysis or Godown Summary, and Cash/Funds Flow (month-per-row tables) do not take them.

features.name: F5 Detailed/Condensed toggle (explode)
features.ours: F5 toggles Detailed/Condensed in Balance Sheet and P&L (detail rows are display-only and never change a total). Shift+Enter explodes the row under the cursor in place in Trial Balance, Group Summary, Balance Sheet, P&L, Stock Summary and the cost reports, recursive to any depth and display-only; every explodable table reserves a small caret slot in its first column.

features.name: Range filter (Alt+F12)
features.ours: Alt+F12 opens a row-filter panel on an Amount or a date range (with AND/OR and one nested group) on the Day Book, every voucher register, Ledger Vouchers and Receivables/Payables. It runs before the report totals its rows, so totals, percentage columns, Print, CSV and Excel follow it; the total row reads 'Total (filtered)' and a bar shows chips, 'N of M rows' and a Filtered badge. A filtered Ledger Vouchers keeps the true Closing Balance and adds 'Other vouchers (not shown)'. A live filter is never saved; a saved view can carry it. Partial: it is not on Trial Balance, Group Summary, Balance Sheet, P&L, Stock Summary, the GST, TDS or payroll reports or about 35 other report files, so 'closing greater than X' on a ledger or group is not available. Built and reviewed in Phase 26 (committed c0d9aa3 and deployed 2026-10-20); never compared with a live TallyPrime. Next: one registry entry (core/reportFilterFields.ts) and one useRowFilter call per report.

features.name: Value/name filter (Ctrl+F12)
features.ours: Ctrl+F12 opens the same panel on a name or value condition (contains, does not contain, starts with, is exactly; is / is not for a fixed list) on the Day Book, every voucher register, Ledger Vouchers and Receivables/Payables; conditions combine with AND/OR and the report's totals follow them. features.name: Scale factor / units display (thousands/lakhs)
features.ours: F12 scale (Units/Thousands/Lakhs) live in Trial Balance, Balance Sheet, P&L (single + comparative columns), godown/movement reports. Live-verified 10,000 -> 10.00 in Thousands.

The sub line says what each percentage is a percentage OF; each comparative column uses its own base; a zero base shows blank, never 0% or NaN.

features.name: Report printing (Alt+P / preview)
features.tally: Print any report with page setup/titles.
features.ours: Ctrl/Cmd+P prints the visible report through the browser: the screen chrome is removed, the colour tokens re-point at paper so a dark screen prints like a light one, and table headers repeat (reportTools.ts, print/fit.ts).

features.name: Export report (Excel/PDF/CSV/JSON)
features.ours: Print and Export act on any report table (reportTools.ts reads the visible .scr-body). A report now exports as CSV (one writer, csvOut: a cell starting = + - or @ gets an apostrophe) and as a real .xlsx (core/xlsx.ts and core/reportSheet.ts: pure OOXML in a store-only zip; text is never a formula; figures are numbers and dates are Excel dates; column widths, a title block, the header row kept in view and a dressed total row); the old HTML table named .xls, which nothing called, is gone. Alt+F9 saves a PDF (see export-pdf). Partial: JSON, XML, HTML and image export are not built; the .xlsx was checked with unzip -t, xmllint and this app's own reader, never opened in real Excel, LibreOffice or Google Sheets. Phase 29: built and reviewed, deployed 2026-10-23 (BETA; authenticated cloud flows not exercised on the VM).

features.name: Email / share report
features.ours: The Share panel (Alt+M, the top-bar M) works from a voucher, its print preview, a party's bills or ledger, or a party list. WhatsApp (a wa.me link) and e-mail (mailto) only OPEN the person's own app with the message ready; nothing is sent from here and the panel says so. It copies the text, offers the browser's share sheet (Web Share, with a file where the browser allows), and, because a mailto link cannot attach a file, offers the Excel statement or the PDF first. A role without the view right gets the reason and no figures; the desktop app validates links in share:open. Partial against Tally's e-mail from the report screen: nothing is sent or attached by the app, no templates, and the Web Share path and the desktop share:open path were not driven for real (the harness has neither). The WhatsApp link rule is from vendor guides quoting WhatsApp's help page, which could not be fetched. Phase 29: built and reviewed, deployed 2026-10-23 (BETA; authenticated cloud flows not exercised on the VM).

features.name: Cancelled Vouchers register
features.ours: Alt+X cancels a voucher and KEEPS ITS NUMBER, from the Day Book, every voucher register and the voucher being altered (also the header '...' menu and a rail button). It asks why (a reason is required, cleaned and capped), then asks again with Keep armed. A cancelled voucher is a shell (Voucher.cancelled plus optional: true, no lines, party or flags), so it posts nothing: 20 engines (balances, P&L, balance sheet, stock, bills, GSTR-1/3B/9, registers, dashboard, TDS register, Tally XML and more) give the same answer as if it had never existed, asserted, including after an older client flips optional off (the store seals it). Its number is never reused, and GSTR-1 Table 13 and the doc_issue JSON count it as cancelled (a number that was only deleted stays a gap). The Cancelled / Deleted register lists both with a status badge and the reason. A cancelled voucher opens read-only (who, when, why), is never printed, shared, bulk-printed or exported as a real invoice, and cannot be altered or un-cancelled (as in TallyPrime): delete stays, with No armed, and Ctrl+Z straight after is the only way back (two steps for a reverse-charge purchase, whose Journal is removed with it). The reason prompt warns about a registered IRN (cancel on the portal within 24 hours or raise a credit note), a live e-way bill, bills settled against it and bank-reconciled lines. On the cloud a cancelled voucher stays cancelled: another device's stale edit is set aside in the Sync Mismatch Report and that device is told (the server rule, backend/src/conflict.js, was deployed 2026-10-23 and has not been exercised on the VM). Not built: un-cancel, Alt+X on the Ledger Vouchers drill, bulk cancel (one voucher at a time), ISCANCELLED in Tally XML (import skips and counts them, export omits and counts them), cancelling an IRN or an e-way bill through a portal. Not compared with a live TallyPrime, the GST portal or the IRP. Phase 29: built and reviewed, deployed 2026-10-23 (BETA; authenticated cloud flows not exercised on the VM).

features.name: Auto BRS via bank statement import
features.ours: Import Bank Statement (BRS, key I) reads CSV/TSV (UTF-8/UTF-16/Windows-1252), pasted Excel rows, MT940 and CAMT.053 into neutral StatementLines, matches them one-to-one against unreconciled entries (reference+amount, then amount+date window, then unique amount; ambiguous lines are never auto-ticked), shows a review screen, then stamps the Bank Dates as one batch with Ctrl+Z undo that lasts only while the screen stays open. Re-import is idempotent; altering a stamped voucher no longer drops its Bank Date. Partial: .xlsx/.xls/.pdf are not read (Save As CSV or paste); fixtures are reconstructions, not real bank exports; one-to-many matches are not attempted.

features.name: Bank statement format configuration
features.ours: Columns are detected from header synonyms and proved against the data (dates parse, amounts are numbers, running balance agrees, swapped Debit/Credit is caught). M opens a keyboard map (header row, date format, value date, narration, cheque/ref, split Debit/Credit or one Amount with sign/Dr-Cr, balance) with a live preview; the layout is saved on the bank ledger (Ledger.stmtFormat) so the next import of that bank is one key. A real statement per bank is still needed to harden the synonyms.

features.name: Create/link vouchers from statement rows
features.ours: V on a statement line the books lack plans a plain two-ledger Payment/Receipt (or Contra), counter ledger suggested from earlier choices and never invented (or created inline), born reconciled with the statement date as Bank Date, reference as instrument number, the bank's wording as narration, numbered like the voucher screen, never optional. L links an existing unreconciled entry instead; U applies every suggestion; re-import cannot duplicate them. No GST, TDS, bill or cost-centre allocation (said on screen).

features.name: Cheque printing from payment voucher
features.ours: Cheque printing from the payment voucher and the Cheque Register (Banking > C): a per-bank layout in millimetres, live scaled preview, Ctrl+P ruler-grid test sheet, page set to the leaf size with no margin; a cheque prints its instrument date. A cheque is marked printed once window.print() returns (a cancelled dialog cannot be detected).

features.name: Bank-wise cheque printing config
features.ours: Each bank ledger has its own cheque layout in millimetres: leaf size (four nominal presets or custom), position, width and font size of every field, 7 date formats (optional per-digit boxes), figure style, characters per words line with an overflow warning, and a calibration shift. No bank's real leaf specification ships (a generic editable starting point; the CTS-2010 size is unchecked against the RBI standard); alignment can only be confirmed by a test print over a real leaf.

features.name: Payee/favouring name & A/c Payee crossing
features.ours: Party ledgers gain a 'Cheque favouring name' (in the Registration & Cheque Details block after Opening Balance). The Cheque Register sets each cheque's favouring name and crossing (bank default, A/C PAYEE, A/C PAYEE + NOT NEGOTIABLE, NOT NEGOTIABLE, & CO., Bearer, Order, None). The payee falls back from the cheque's own name to the party's favouring name to the ledger name; a self cheque is made out to 'Self' and never crossed; editing a printed cheque shows 'Changed since'.

features.name: Cheque register report
features.ours: Cheque Register lists cheque payments and Contras (incl. Bank OD ledgers) with the per-cheque favouring name, crossing and printed mark, and flags each row Reused, Cancelled leaf or Not in a book.

features.name: Cheque book management (ranges/availability)
features.ours: Cheque Books screen (Banking > K): several books per bank (series prefix, first and last leaf, zero-padding kept, cancelled-leaf list such as '105, 110-112'); used, cancelled and available counts come from the cheque payments, never typed. A leaf map shows each leaf's state and the next to use; overlapping or bad ranges are refused; choosing Cheque at entry fills the next leaf (editable). Books live on the bank ledger, so two devices altering one ledger at once is last-writer-wins.

features.name: Blank/available cheque tracking & alerts

features.tally: Mark a range reconciled with one date.
features.ours: In Bank Reconciliation, Space and Shift+arrows mark rows; D sets one bank date on the marked rows (or on every shown row with no bank date), C clears it on marked rows only. features.name: Company password / Tally Vault (encryption)
features.ours: Opening a protected company needs its passcode, stored only as a salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hash (pure-JS fallback for plain-http deploys), asked at boot, desktop start, Select Company and switching; a wrong one loads nothing. Old plaintext passcodes and PINs become hashes on first unlock, on alteration, on restore and in every exported copy; an old passcode that was never enforced no longer locks anyone out (a one-time prompt keeps or drops it). A restore over a passcode-protected company that is not open here is refused. Partial: nothing is encrypted (the books are readable in IndexedDB; backups are plain JSON minus the secrets), and a forgotten company passcode cannot be reset.

features.name: Security control master toggle
features.ours: Security control is opt-in (F12 on Security) and enforced where data is written: save, delete, restore, Mark Optional/Regular, bank dates and undo. Turning it on shows a one-time recovery key for forgotten PINs. Client-side control only: the books remain readable in IndexedDB and the sync server does not enforce roles (the screens say so).

features.name: Administrator / Owner account
features.tally: Owner has full rights, manages users.
features.ours: The Owner (and any Administration user) must have a PIN and has full rights; lock-out guards keep at least one administrator who can sign in. The company passcode is never accepted in place of a PIN.

features.name: Users master (create/alter/delete)
features.tally: Named users mapped to security levels.
features.ours: The Security screen lists named operators with a PIN, each mapped to a role; operators change their own PIN on Sign In (Alt+P, current PIN first). Users in non-admin roles may have no PIN (marked 'no PIN'), so their Edit Log stamps prove nothing.

features.name: Security levels / roles
features.tally: Reusable rights templates assigned to users.
features.ours: Roles limit areas, voucher types, create/alter/delete and a date window; the company period lock applies to roles without full access. Menus, palette and sidebar hide what the operator cannot open.

features.name: Rights matrix (allow/disallow per report & action)
features.ours: Rights are per area plus voucher type and create/alter/delete, refused before Accept and Delete. There is no per-report or Print right. Every new screen needs a SCREEN_AREA entry (core/access.ts) or it is admin-only.

features.name: Voucher-type / period access restriction
features.tally: Restrict user to voucher types and date range.
features.ours: Each role is limited by areas, voucher types, create/alter/delete and a date window; the company period lock applies to roles without full access. Enforced at the write path (save, delete, restore, Mark Optional, bank dates, undo); the Edit Log records the operator. With security off, behaviour is byte-for-byte as before. Payroll, attendance, e-invoice and Alt+C ledger creation have no early check: a refused save shows the reason and writes nothing.

features.name: Password policy & change password
features.ours: One shared rule set (at least 8 characters, not common, not a run, keyboard row or repeat, and not the email): the backend enforces it on /auth/register and on a new signed-in, rate-limited /auth/change-password (checks the current password, signs out every other session); Sync Settings has a strength meter and Change Password (Alt+P). Old short passwords still log in. The check returns at once on over-long input (a quadratic pattern once froze the server for minutes). Partial: no expiry or reuse history. LIVE on the VM since 2026-10-19: weak passwords are refused on register and a wrong current password is refused on /auth/change-password (verified against the deployed server).

features.name: Remote users / Tally.NET authorized users
features.tally: Named remote users with own rights.
features.ours: No remote-user concept.

features.name: Edit Log / audit trail (old-vs-new, user)
features.tally: Every change with user, timestamp, old-vs-new.
features.ours: Every change is logged to the outbox change-log; the Edit Log names the signed-in operator, a restore's deletes carry the operator, and system writes (migrations, PIN hashing) are stamped operator 'System', never a user action.

features.name: Edit Log report & version drill-down
features.tally: Browse edit history, drill each version.
features.ours: No edit-log report UI.

features.name: Deleted/cancelled voucher tracking
features.ours: The Cancelled / Deleted register (Reports Center, Go To) lists vouchers DELETED on this device, rebuilt from its change-log (deleted-on, type, no, date, party, amount, deleted by: now the operator rather than the sync account), and the vouchers CANCELLED with their number kept, each with a status badge and the reason; a cancelled-then-deleted voucher reads Deleted and says it had been cancelled. Partial: the deletions come from this device's own change-log, so a voucher deleted on another device is not listed here (cancelled vouchers are voucher rows and do sync). Not compared with a live TallyPrime's audit view. Phase 29: built and reviewed, deployed 2026-10-23 (BETA; authenticated cloud flows not exercised on the VM).

features.name: Backup company data
features.ours: exportCompany JSON (tallyweb-backup-v2) with schemaVersion, appVersion and per-table row counts; operator PINs and the company passcode appear only as salted hashes, never plaintext (the books themselves are not encrypted). Manual backup needs the Administration right when security control is on.

features.name: Restore company data
features.ours: Restore validates first (damaged, truncated, newer-app or foreign-company files are refused before anything is deleted), shows what the file holds and what it replaces (default No), and, because restore means replace, queues deletes for rows the file lacks so a restore of an older backup reaches the cloud and other devices (operator-stamped, not an undo step). A company with a passcode that is not open here refuses a restore.

features.name: Scheduled / automatic backup
features.ours: Backup / Restore sets an automatic schedule per company (Daily / Weekly / when the company is closed / Off), how many to keep and a backup folder. The desktop app writes through a validated IPC bridge, Chrome/Edge to a chosen folder; a file is read back before 'Last backup' is stamped and older automatic backups rotate out (never the newest); a 'Backup due' banner offers Back up now. With security control on, a manual backup needs the Administration right (other roles see a button-less notice). Limits: the Electron half is checked only against a mocked electron and needs an installer rebuild; other browsers download on B and never back up automatically; schedule and last-backup record are per device.

features.name: Cloud / continuous multi-device sync
features.ours: Node+SQLite server: auth, append-only log, push/pull cursor, device-echo suppression.

features.name: Split company data by period
features.tally: Split by date carrying closing as opening.
features.ours: Split Company Data (Company menu Z, Go To, palette) makes two new companies from the open one at a split date (financial-year start by default), leaving the original untouched, carrying the closing position as openings: ledger balances, P&L result, bills on original dates, stock by godown and batch, bank balance, pending orders, numbering, cheque books. The engine proves the split ties out (Balance Sheet, trial balance, stock, bills, bank) before offering it; it is refused if the books changed after they were read, the sync pull is held during review, and it is administrator-only. New companies carry no passcode or sign-in. Limits (listed on screen): FIFO/LIFO layers and the last purchase rate are carried at a blended rate, cost-centre openings, deductee-wise TDS/TCS detail, payroll year-to-date, leave balances and GST/TDS turnover aggregates do not carry.

features.name: Rewrite company (repair)
features.ours: Data Check (Company menu H, Go To, palette) checks the open company for missing reserved masters, records pointing at missing masters, ledgers with no group, group loops, unbalanced vouchers (Optional only as warnings), duplicate master names, duplicate voucher numbers per numbering window and change-log anomalies; Enter opens the record; R previews and re-creates missing masters as one step undone with Ctrl+Z. It never deletes or rewrites anything, and does not check TDS/TCS nature, price-level or CRM/HR references.

features.name: Migrate / auto-upgrade data on version change
features.tally: Auto-migrates older data to current format.
features.ours: Backups carry schemaVersion, appVersion and per-table row counts (format tag unchanged). On restore an older file is migrated step by step; a file from a newer app, a damaged, truncated or foreign-company file is refused before anything is deleted; the person sees what the file holds and what it replaces and is asked (default No), on Backup / Restore (R) and Import Data (C).

features.name: Export to XML (Tally native)
features.ours: Export Data (Company menu X, Go To, palette) writes the masters and the period's transactions as two TallyPrime import-format XML files (parents before children; stock journals, delivery/receipt notes and physical counts included; optional vouchers left out); a party's GST identity is written truthfully (Indian state with country India, a named country with state Not Applicable, no invented country); after each download the screen lists what could not be carried. The sample company round-trips to identical books. Partial: never imported into a live TallyPrime (field tags unverified); importing the same file twice there duplicates vouchers (no GUID written); no CSV/Excel layout (TallyPrime imports Excel only, through its own mapping template). A cancelled voucher is left out of the export with a count (ISCANCELLED is not written).

features.name: Import from XML (masters & vouchers)
features.tally: Bulk import masters/transactions from Tally XML.
features.ours: Imports a TallyPrime XML export (UTF-16, UTF-8 or Windows-1252), repairs the  markers, and shows a preview (counts, repairs, each voucher refused with its reason) before saving; Enter saves everything in one transaction: groups, units, ledgers (opening bills, GST and bank details), stock groups, godowns, stock items with HSN/GST history, cost categories/centres, accounting vouchers with bill-wise/cost-centre/godown/batch detail and per-line GST where the file carries it, stock journals, delivery/receipt notes, physical stock. Additive; it only fills a nil opening on an existing ledger. Not imported (counted): orders, rejection/job-work types, payroll/attendance, multi-currency, stock-journal additional-cost lines. SEZ/Deemed Export are not restored. Never run on a file from a live TallyPrime. A voucher marked ISCANCELLED is skipped and counted, not imported as a kept-number cancelled voucher.

features.name: Export to PDF
features.ours: Alt+F9 on a report, a voucher's print preview or bulk print. In a browser the key opens the print window and the status line names Save as PDF as the destination to choose (a page cannot write a PDF). In the desktop app electron/exportBridge.cjs (pdf:save) writes the PDF through webContents.printToPDF behind a validated IPC bridge: it takes a name and two options, never a path, writes only to the path chosen in the save dialog (.part then rename, %PDF check, size check, one save at a time); the appId, the userData pin and contextIsolation are asserted unchanged. Partial: the real printToPDF and save dialog were NEVER run (the Electron binary is not installed here; the bridge was exercised against a fake electron and a fake file system), so rebuild the installers and run it once before shipping; the browser path is still a dialog; no PDF attached to mail, no digital signature. Phase 29: built and reviewed, deployed 2026-10-23 (BETA; authenticated cloud flows not exercised on the VM).

features.name: Export to HTML / JPEG / ASCII
features.ours: Not supported.

features.name: Import from Excel/CSV
features.ours: Import Data > X reads .xlsx and CSV (a minimal OOXML reader with limits against hostile files; the header row is found under a title block; UTF-16 files read) and maps columns by name for ledgers, stock items and vouchers; the mapping is remembered per file shape on this device. A preview with per-row errors comes first and nothing is saved; Enter then writes everything in one transaction tagged as a batch. It is additive and balance-guarded, and a second import of the same file adds nothing. It refuses a total line, a row with no name, a number it cannot read exactly, a date far from the open year, and reads Cr/Dr words, a trailing minus, Excel percent cells (0.18 as 18) and Excel dates; names are cleaned; voucher numbers follow the type's window and format. The CSV import of ledgers, items and vouchers and the Tally XML import are unchanged. Partial: a voucher is ONE two-ledger row (no item or multi-line GST invoices; Bulk Entry covers pasted item vouchers), the old binary .xls is not read, no sample files, and it was checked on files this app's own writer and fixtures made, not on workbooks from other packages. Phase 29: built and reviewed, deployed 2026-10-23 (BETA; authenticated cloud flows not exercised on the VM).
