features.name: Multi-user concurrent access over LAN
features.tally: Several users on same company with locking.
features.ours: Other users' changes arrive in about a second over the live stream the server already pushed (coalesced, backoff with jitter, silent offline, jittered fallback poll). Partial: no presence / who-is-editing list and no on-prem LAN server; multi-user runs through the cloud backend.

features.name: Record locking / concurrency conflict handling
features.tally: Prevents simultaneous edits of same voucher.
features.ours: Two people changing one record out of step no longer overwrite each other silently: every change carries the revision it was based on, the cloud records a mismatch with both versions and a field-level comparison for the owner/admin (Company > Sync Mismatch Report), a pull never overwrites an unsent local edit (the remote version is kept as a mismatch record) or hands a device a version its own later write superseded, and a form left open while a sync rewrites its record warns at Save. Optimistic detection plus a report, not a hard per-voucher lock. Needs backend migration 007 deployed.

features.name: Company logo on invoices/reports
features.ours: Company logo upload (data URL) on create/alter; rendered on invoice + report prints (CompanyBlock).

features.name: Print configuration (paper/margins/copies/title)
features.tally: F12 print config paper size, copies, range, declaration.
features.ours: Print Configuration (F12 on Voucher Printing, or Company > Print Configuration, T) is one keyboard form with a live preview of the latest real voucher of that type: paper (A4/A5/Letter), orientation, margin, title, logo position, copies, and which columns and blocks print (ship-to, HSN, rate, per, unit, discount, GST rate, batch, GST breakup, words, E&OE, bank, terms, jurisdiction, declaration, signature, narration). Saved per voucher type over a company default (only differences stored, synced with the company); an absent setting prints exactly as before. Hiding a part never changes a figure; hiding one a GST tax invoice needs (CGST Rule 46) warns but saves. Not tested outside Chromium/Electron printing; thermal 80mm is out of scope.

features.name: Multi-copy Original/Duplicate/Triplicate
features.tally: Prints copy labels and repeats copies.
features.ours: A copy setting prints the whole document once per copy with the label above the title (page numbers restart per copy): single copy (default), goods triplicate (Rule 48(1)), services duplicate (Rule 48(2)), delivery-challan triplicate (Rule 55(2)) on Delivery Notes, or up to 5 owner-typed labels. Statutory presets apply to Sales (and Delivery Note for the challan set); goods or services is the owner's choice, never guessed. Bulk print (the selection bar's I, Print vouchers) builds each voucher with its own type's paper, copies and labels (Phase 29).

features.name: Company mailing / statutory detail config
features.ours: Alter Company has an Additional Details section: CIN/LLPIN, Udyam no., IEC, website, second phone and jurisdiction city; format checks warn and never block. CIN/LLPIN, Udyam and IEC print beside GSTIN/PAN on both print layouts; 'Subject to X jurisdiction' prints only when a city is entered; the declaration is shown pre-filled and editable per voucher type.

features.name: Licensing / activation / subscription tiers
features.ours: Serial licensing is replaced by SaaS: 7-day trials, plans and subscription status gate cloud sync (canSync, entitlement 402 read-only lockout), with a Subscription screen and an admin portal. Payments are MOCK (no live Razorpay keys) and plan max_companies/max_users are display-only (nothing enforces them); a hidden zero-price 'unlimited' plan exists for comped accounts.

features.name: Multiple company management & shut
features.ours: CompanySelect/Create/Alter/Shut + F3 switch.

features.name: Group company / consolidation
features.ours: Multi-company exists; no consolidation across companies.

features.name: F11 company feature toggles
features.ours: F11 Company Features screen toggles all these.

features.name: Data folder / path configuration
features.ours: Fixed IndexedDB store; no configurable path.

features.name: TDL developer customization / add-ons
features.tally: Load TDL/TCP add-ons for fields/reports without recompiling.
features.ours: No TDL loader or plugin layer; code edits required. The no-code custom fields (the live v1, b-udf, and v2, merged into main as 1d22e84 and not deployed, b-custom-fields) are not TDL: they add fields to masters and vouchers and reports by field, not Tally add-ons, so this row stays missing.

buildOrderNext.why: Portal-shaped is not filing-grade: try a real import in the offline tool and settle the SCHEMA? fields (hsn_b2b/hsn_b2c keys, WOPAY rate, CDNR original-invoice reference, 3B itc_rev/itc_inelg codes).
The importer and exporter are proven on hand-built fixtures only; one run on a real TallyPrime export decides whether migration works.
About 35 report files (GST returns, TDS, payroll statements) are not on F12 yet; each needs one useF12(title, spec) call.
Only the passcode half exists; encrypted backups and at-rest encryption need TLS or a pure-JS cipher.
Manufacture hardcodes Main Location, captures no batch/expiry and values FIFO items at average cost.
A native .xlsx reader now exists (core/xlsxRead.ts, used by Import Data) but is not wired into Import Bank Statement; one real statement per bank would take statement import from partial to covered.
Freight and loading on a purchase never reach the item's cost, so closing stock and gross profit are understated for traders.
No TDS on salary (s.192): the largest missing payroll computation.
Every item invoice has its GST ledger rows picked by hand; a class presets them.
The job-work chain (Material Out/In, orders, job-worker godown, registers) is wholly absent.
BOM is a flat array set once on first manufacture; no named or multiple BOMs, and per-unit quantity is rounded.
An increment rewrites the past for statutory and gratuity reports.
Phase 2 (IRP/GSP relay) needs TLS, a credential vault and a partner contract before IRNs can be generated here.

The backend half was deployed 2026-10-23 (backend/sql/008_voucher_series.sql applied, numbering.js, sync.js, conflict.js; the routes answer 401 without a token). Still to do: smoke-test signed in on the VM, two reserves with one key (same number), a claim of a held number (taken) and a 402 trial lock; the route wrapper has never run signed in on a real server and two real devices have never met.

Upload the bulk file to the portal's offline tool and import a real results file: the key names and version tag come from ERPNext's generator and a Vayana sample, and 8 rules rest on secondary sources (EWB_UNCERTAIN). Live generation and cancel need a GSP.

Run the desktop PDF write once for real (electron/exportBridge.cjs, never run: the Electron binary was not installed) and rebuild the Windows and Mac installers; no browser can write the file without a dialog.
A blocking mode and the check on accounting-mode vouchers (Journal, Payment, Receipt, Sales as voucher); Bulk Entry only warns and takes no reason.

roadmapEpics.why: An integration surface is the platform moat Tally lacks natively; it makes TallyWeb the system-of-record other apps build on and drives sticky ecosystem revenue.
roadmapEpics.scope: Versioned REST for masters/vouchers/reports, scoped API keys, OAuth2 client-credentials, rate limits, pagination, idempotency keys, OpenAPI docs + sandbox.
roadmapEpics.shippedNote: Scoped keys + versioned /v1 REST, surfaced in-app (Phase 19).

roadmapEpics.why: Push events (voucher.created, stock.low, payment.received) let customers automate workflows and integrators react in real time — table-stakes for modern SaaS.
roadmapEpics.scope: Event bus, subscription management, signed payloads (HMAC), retries with backoff + dead-letter, delivery logs and replay UI.
roadmapEpics.shippedNote: HMAC-signed outbound webhooks with retry + de-dup, plus a delivery log (Phase 19).

roadmapEpics.epic: Custom fields (UDF) on any object + in reports
roadmapEpics.why: Replaces Tally's TDL developer barrier with no-code user-defined fields, making the product self-serviceable and defensible against verticalized competitors.
roadmapEpics.scope: UDF schema per object (ledger/item/voucher/employee), typed fields + validation, render in forms, filter/sort/column them in reports and exports, API exposure.
roadmapEpics.shippedNote: Shipped on ledgers and stock items; NOT yet surfaced in reports.

roadmapEpics.why: Cloud-native collaboration (approve a voucher, @mention an accountant, assign follow-ups) is something desktop Tally structurally cannot offer.
roadmapEpics.scope: Threaded comments on vouchers/masters, @mentions + notifications, task assignment, maker-checker approval workflow with audit ties.

roadmapEpics.why: The current single-account SQLite sync server cannot serve many orgs securely; a real multi-tenant backend is the prerequisite for every other SaaS epic.
roadmapEpics.scope: Tenant isolation + row-level security, Postgres migration, horizontal scaling, encryption at rest/in transit, backups/DR, SSO/SAML, audit logging, SOC2 posture.
roadmapEpics.shippedNote: Fastify + Postgres with RLS tenancy, deployed. See HANDOFF §2 for the trust map.

roadmapEpics.why: Directly monetizes the SaaS with recurring revenue and self-serve growth, replacing Tally's perpetual-license + TSS model.
roadmapEpics.scope: Plan/tier management, seat + usage metering, Stripe/Razorpay, trials, dunning, invoices/GST on our own billing, entitlement gating tied to feature flags.
roadmapEpics.shippedNote: 7-day trials, subscriptions and entitlement lockout. Payments are still MOCK.

roadmapEpics.why: Owners want on-the-go dashboards, invoice creation and approvals; mobile is a decisive differentiator and drives daily engagement.
roadmapEpics.scope: React Native app sharing core logic, offline-first sync, biometric login, invoice/receipt capture, dashboards, approvals + push notifications.

roadmapEpics.why: Expands ACV by owning the full employee lifecycle on top of existing payroll, competing with standalone HR suites.
roadmapEpics.scope: Leave & attendance management, employee self-service portal, onboarding/offboarding, documents, expense claims, PF/ESI/PT/IT statutory built on the payroll engine.
roadmapEpics.shippedNote: Leave types, applications, approvals and live balances (Phase 18).

roadmapEpics.why: Connecting leads-to-invoice keeps sales and finance in one system, increasing stickiness and cross-sell versus point CRMs.
roadmapEpics.scope: Contacts/leads/opportunities, pipeline stages, quotations flowing into sales orders/invoices, activity timeline, email integration, sales dashboards.

roadmapEpics.why: Cloud data enables live, shareable dashboards and proactive alerts that a desktop ledger tool cannot, raising perceived value for owners/CFOs.
roadmapEpics.scope: Configurable KPI dashboards, drill-through, saved views, scheduled email/WhatsApp digests, anomaly alerts, embed/share links.
roadmapEpics.shippedNote: Customisable Dashboard (15 widgets, per operator plus a company layout) and saved report views shipped in Phase 24. Phase 26 (deployed 2026-10-20) added a Reports Center, a row filter and views shared company-wide. Phase 28 (committed 5c94342 and deployed 2026-10-21, BETA) rebuilds the Dashboard as a period-aware board of 22 widgets with charts, as-at figures and drill-through (b-dashboard-v2); view widgets wait for the grid query core. Scheduled digests, anomaly alerts and share links are not built.

beyond.name: Ghost recall (prefix-addressable prior voucher)
beyond.note: Type four letters of a party and the shape of their last voucher appears; Ctrl+Space (Alt+R on Mac) materialises it, re-derived against today's masters with changed list prices badged. Bills and instruments deliberately dropped. Tally, Busy and Marg all offer only static templates or a blind copy.

beyond.name: Superset amount & date fields
beyond.note: Amounts take arithmetic (1250*18/100) and Indian shorthand (25k, 1.5L, 2.3cr); dates take the QuickBooks/Intacct letter set (t, m/h, y/r, w/k, +N). Quantities share the arithmetic but never the magnitudes — L is Litre. A plain number behaves exactly as before.

beyond.name: Undo (Ctrl+Z) on the change log
beyond.note: Ctrl+A is final with no prompt (as in TallyPrime); Ctrl+Z reverses the data afterwards and leaves a create-then-void pair for the auditor. Confirmation dialogs taxed every action to catch a rare mistake.

beyond.name: Command palette with user aliases
beyond.note: Raycast-style deterministic tiers; user aliases on ledgers and stock items matched prefix-only ('rt' -> Ramesh Traders); scope prefixes; keycaps that teach the Tally key. Destructive commands are exact-prefix only and frecency can never move the top row.

beyond.name: Bulk entry — paste a block from Excel
beyond.note: One row per voucher, every voucher-screen guard enforced per row, committed as one atomic transaction and one undo step. Matters disproportionately in India, where a client hands the accountant a spreadsheet that is currently retyped.

beyond.name: Pinned batch constants (Alt+K)
beyond.note: Holds Party / Godown / Place-of-Supply across the post-save reset — SAP's Hold Data, the overwritable variant. Every hold is named on screen; a value carried invisibly is how a batch lands in the wrong GST state.

beyond.name: Today / Pinned / Recent rail
beyond.note: Replaced a rail that duplicated the menu tree. Shows what a menu tree cannot: what was actually entered today, pinned screens, and recents — per company. Since Phase 25 this is the Quick access view of the left rail; the default view is the module menu (b-menu).

beyond.name: Searchable key sheet, hold-Alt reveal, G-chords
beyond.note: '?' opens a searchable sheet defaulting to the current screen. Holding Alt badges the driving key on the element itself. G+letter reaches the screens that never had F-keys, and yields to any screen that binds bare G.

beyond.name: CRM pipeline
beyond.note: Leads through new/qualified/quoted/won with follow-ups; a won lead links to the party ledger, so the pipeline and the books share one customer.

beyond.name: HR leave management
beyond.note: Leave types, applications, approvals and live balances on the existing payroll, with overlap guards. Unpaid leave flows to loss-of-pay without a second system.

beyond.name: Open platform — API keys, REST, webhooks
beyond.note: Scoped keys, a versioned REST API and HMAC-signed webhooks, surfaced in-app. Tally needs its XML gateway and, for customisation, a TDL developer.

beyond.name: Custom fields without a developer
beyond.note: Add fields to ledgers and stock items from a settings screen. This is the single thing Tally users pay a consultant for most often.

beyond.name: Mac, browser and multi-device sync
beyond.note: Native Windows AND Mac desktop apps plus any browser, local-first with automatic sync. No server to configure, no ODBC, no remote-access licence.

beyond.name: Type-to-filter in every report
beyond.note: '/' (Ctrl+F) narrows any report's rows live; Indian digit grouping folded so 125000 finds 1,25,000.00. Totals stay whole and are labelled 'totals unfiltered'. The structured row filter added in Phase 26 (b-row-filter) is a different tool: its totals DO follow the filter and are labelled 'Total (filtered)'.

beyond.name: One feedback lane with Undo button
beyond.note: Five competing message systems became one: errors, confirmations and the undo offer share a single position and voice.

beyond.name: Tax invoice & print design
beyond.note: A4 tax invoice with per-rate GST breakup, amount in words, paginated tables; terms and bank accounts print only if the owner chose them.

beyond.name: Selection-scoped actions in registers
beyond.note: Mark rows, then print, export, or mark Optional/Regular as ONE undoable batch. Never deletes, never changes a type or an amount.

beyond.name: First-run welcome and sample company
beyond.note: A new device is offered a realistic, balanced sample company (never synced, deletable), Tally/CSV import, or a blank start — plus a Getting Started checklist that ticks itself from real state.

beyond.name: Narration snippets
beyond.note: ;pmt expands to a template with voucher variables; unfilled blanks refuse Accept. Per device.

beyond.name: Favourite shortcuts (Ctrl+Alt+1..9)
beyond.note: Nine user-assignable jump slots in a chord family nothing else uses, so they can never shadow a Tally key.

beyond.name: Speed-budget harness
beyond.note: npm run perf times the real engines against deterministic 2k/50k/250k-voucher companies and fails when a budget is blown.

beyond.name: Ghost recall for Payment/Receipt/Journal/Contra
beyond.note: Recalls the shape of last month's entry keyed on the first ledger; a recalled bill-wise row must pass the bill panel before it can be accepted.

beyond.name: Operator model and company passcode
beyond.note: Operators sign in with a PIN; roles limit areas, voucher types, create/alter/delete and a date window, enforced where data is written (save, delete, restore, Mark Optional, bank dates, undo), and menus, palette and sidebar hide what an operator cannot open. A one-time recovery key covers a forgotten PIN; the company passcode is stored only as a salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hash. System writes (migrations, PIN hashing) are stamped 'System', never a user action. TallyPrime has users, security levels and a company password: those equivalents are counted in the parity rows (access-restriction, roles, company-vault), so this entry claims only the Comsky-specific design. It is a client-side control: the books stay readable in IndexedDB and the sync server does not enforce roles.

beyond.name: Sync mismatch report
beyond.note: When two devices change one record out of step, the cloud keeps both versions with a field-level comparison for the owner or admin (Company > Sync Mismatch Report). A pull never overwrites an unsent local edit, a form left open over a synced change warns at Save, a restore that would delete cloud records says so, and other users' changes arrive in about a second over the live stream. Optimistic detection plus a report, not a hard lock. Needs backend migration 007 deployed.

beyond.name: Comsky-vs-Tally checker
beyond.note: Compare with Tally Data loads XML exports from the other software and compares them with the open company without writing anything: counts by voucher type and month, voucher-by-voucher matching with drill, ledger and group closing balances, stock, GST totals by month, and a CSV of every difference. A self-test writes our own export, reads it back and compares. Never run on a file from a live TallyPrime; report-style Day Book exports are refused.

beyond.name: Customisable dashboard and saved report views
beyond.note: The Phase 24 build, deployed 2026-10-19 (its Dashboard half has been replaced on the live site by Dashboard v2 since 2026-10-21). The Dashboard is a 12-column board of 15 widgets the operator chooses, orders and sizes from a keyboard edit mode (F12), per operator, with an administrator-set company layout. Alt+V on any F12 report saves its setup (options, sort, added columns, basis, optionally the period) as a named view, recalled from the report, Go To or the sidebar. Views are kept per device, not synced and not per operator; since Phase 26 (deployed 2026-10-20) a view can also carry a row filter and be shared company-wide (b-shared-views). The Dashboard half of this row is replaced by Dashboard v2 (b-dashboard-v2: 22 widgets, charts, as-at figures, a new default board), committed as 5c94342 and deployed 2026-10-21; the saved report views half is unchanged by it.

beyond.name: Backup scheduling and Data Check
beyond.note: Automatic per-company backups (daily, weekly or on close) to a chosen folder with rotation, read-back before 'Last backup' is stamped and a 'Backup due' banner; restore validates the file and the passcode before deleting anything. Data Check finds missing masters, orphan references, group loops, unbalanced vouchers, duplicate numbers and change-log anomalies and repairs missing masters additively as one Ctrl+Z step. The Tally-equivalent parts are counted in scheduled-backup, data-migration and data-rewrite; the Electron half needs an installer rebuild.

beyond.name: Invoice customiser
beyond.note: Print Configuration is one keyboard form with a live preview of the latest real voucher of that type: paper, orientation, margins, title, logo position, copies and every column and block; saved per voucher type over a company default and synced. It warns when a part a GST tax invoice needs (CGST Rule 46) is hidden, and offers the statutory copy sets (Rules 48(1), 48(2), 55(2)). The Tally-equivalent is counted in print-config and print-copies.

beyond.name: Module menu with full-screen view
beyond.note: The left rail has two views behind a Menu | Quick access control: a module Menu (the default) and the old Today / Pinned / Recent. One chord, Ctrl+\ (Cmd+\ on a Mac), the Hide menu button at the start of the breadcrumb, or the hamburger hides the rail for a full-screen view; the choice is remembered per device. The Menu has a filter box that also matches Tally and Zoho names, links into the Gateway submenus, and hides rows by company feature switch or operator rights. Phase 25 shipped it with 14 groups and 108 rows and it was DEPLOYED to the VM on 2026-10-19 (that is the tree the live site still has). Phase 26 replaced the tree with menu v2 (b-menu-v2: 12 groups, 64 rows, a + per row); the control, filter, full-screen view and rights behaviour described here are unchanged. Built for owners and accountants arriving from Zoho Books and other online ERPs (that comparison is from memory, not re-checked against those products); no Tally keys or menu positions changed. BETA: never used by a customer; checked in headless Chrome on macOS only, real key presses on Windows, Linux, Firefox, Safari and Electron are unchecked. Not counted in the parity percentage.

beyond.name: Menu v2: 12 groups, a + on each row
beyond.note: Replaces the Phase 25 tree in the left rail's Menu view. 12 groups (Dashboard, Sales, Purchases, Banking, Accounting, Inventory, Reports, Taxes & Compliance, Payroll & HR, CRM, Data & Utilities, Settings; Pinned on top and Saved views between Reports and Taxes) and 64 rows, each opening a real register or report, 26 of them carrying a + that opens the matching entry screen, and 10 footer links into the Gateway submenus. A click on a group label opens that module's list; the chevron alone expands; Enter on a header opens it, Space toggles it; the + is always visible on the lit row and on touch. All 108 rows of the Phase 25 tree stay reachable (55 on the rail, 14 as a +, 30 in the Reports Center, 9 in Gateway submenus, counted by script when the spec was written), and Go To now also finds every menu label as printed (twelve, such as Credit Notes, Ledgers and Journals, answered 'No matches' before). The left-menu + opens its form on top of the list so Esc returns to it. Tally keys stay as dim keycaps on 9 rows; the voucher F-keys moved into the + tooltip. A clerk keeps the Reports Center as a one-row group. Not done: a pristine voucher with a held party (Alt+K) still counts as dirty, so a rail click asks. Supersedes the tree of docs/design/left-nav-spec.md; spec docs/design/zoho-ux-spec.md. BETA: built, reviewed, committed (c0d9aa3) and deployed 2026-10-20 (web app only), never used by a customer; checked in headless Chrome on macOS only. Not counted in the parity percentage.

beyond.name: Universal + and one create registry
beyond.note: A + in the top bar, right of the Go To pill, opens a five-column menu of every create (Sales, Purchases, Banking and Accounting, Inventory, General with Payroll and CRM). The 28 creates live in ONE registry (src/ui/quickCreate.ts) that also feeds each left-menu row's + and each page's + New menu, so a create is listed in exactly one place and gated in exactly one way: company feature switches, operator rights and the voucher type's own create right, the same checks the store applies. Chord Alt+Q (Option+Q on a Mac), chosen after auditing every Alt and Ctrl chord in the app; it does nothing inside a text field, behind an overlay, on a gate screen, on key repeat or with Shift, so a half-typed field is never disturbed (the top-bar button and Go To still reach every create from a form). Listed on the ? sheet and in Favourite Shortcuts' locked keys from one chord registry (core/shortcutRegistry.ts). BETA: built, reviewed, committed (c0d9aa3) and deployed 2026-10-20 (web app only), never used by a customer; checked in headless Chrome on macOS only. Not counted in the parity percentage.

beyond.name: + New header and ... menu on lists
beyond.note: Registers, the master pickers, the Chart of Accounts and the reports get one page header (src/ui/pageHeader.tsx, src/ui/header/): a + New menu (the screen's own create first, then its related creates; 33 page entries in the registry), a ... menu (Print, Export CSV or Excel, Configure F12, Save as view, Filter, Import, Bulk Entry, Refresh, as that screen offers them) and a views dropdown in the title (b-shared-views). The Tally F-keys appear in the menus as information only: no F-key is bound on a list and no Tally key changes meaning. While a menu is open it ignores every key but its own, the lit item is exposed to screen readers. Reports Center draws its own Create New Report button instead of a + New. BETA: built, reviewed, committed (c0d9aa3) and deployed 2026-10-20 (web app only), never used by a customer; checked in headless Chrome on macOS only. Not counted in the parity percentage.

beyond.name: Navigation that does not pile up
beyond.note: Fixes the breadcrumb that grew with every left-menu click (reproduced: accept one voucher, click six rail rows, crumb eight deep). Go To was a second source of the same pile-up and is covered. Navigation now decides on real unsaved work: screens register a probe (vouchers, every master and company form, payroll vouchers, Bulk Entry, Import Data, Manufacturing, the budget editor, the report builder; state/dirty.ts). A clean screen is replaced; a screen already in the stack is popped back to instead of repeated; a dirty one asks 'Leave this entry? Entries will be lost.' (Stay is armed; S, N, Esc and Enter stay, L and Y leave). Peeks are capped at 6 and a collapse never drops a dirty entry. The crumb shows its last four segments with the whole path as its tooltip. Verified in the running app on 36 create and alter screens: a dirty voucher is never silently lost, an untouched entry never asks, and Esc inside a voucher keeps its own Quit prompt. BETA: built, reviewed, committed (c0d9aa3) and deployed 2026-10-20 (web app only), never used by a customer; checked in headless Chrome on macOS only. Not counted in the parity percentage.

beyond.name: Row filter on lists and registers
beyond.note: Alt+F12 (an Amount or a date range) and Ctrl+F12 (a name or value) open a filter panel on the Day Book, every voucher register, Ledger Vouchers and Receivables/Payables: text, number, date and fixed-list conditions with AND/OR and one nested group, applied live, and run BEFORE the report totals its rows, so totals, percentage columns, Print, CSV and Excel all follow it. The total row reads 'Total (filtered)', the sub line says 'Filtered: ...' and a bar shows chips, 'N of M rows' and a Filtered badge. A filtered Ledger Vouchers keeps the true Closing Balance and adds 'Other vouchers (not shown)', so opening plus shown plus not shown equals closing. A live filter is never saved (a source scan asserts no storage call); only a saved view carries one (b-shared-views). A saved condition that names a field the report no longer has is kept and matches nothing, never dropped, so a saved view cannot silently widen. Registers also gain a flat 'All vouchers' level behind a By month | All vouchers toggle. TallyPrime has range and value filters: those equivalents are counted in the parity rows report-range-filter and report-value-filter (both still partial, because the filter is not on Trial Balance, the Balance Sheet, P&L, Stock Summary or the GST, TDS and payroll reports), so this entry claims only the design: one panel, saved and shareable, totals that say they are filtered. The earlier '/' type-to-filter (b-filter) is separate. BETA: built, reviewed, committed (c0d9aa3) and deployed 2026-10-20 (web app only), never used by a customer; checked in headless Chrome on macOS only. Not counted in the parity percentage.

beyond.name: Saved views with filters, shareable company-wide
beyond.note: A saved report view (Alt+V, Phase 24) now also carries the row filter, a scope (me or company), a category, its author and a Custom mark. Personal views stay on the device. Company views live on the company row (Company.reportViews, at most 40, written only under the Administration right through the write guard), sync through the change log and survive Alter Company and Split Company Data. The report title carries an 'All' dropdown: Favourites (the left menu's pin: one favourites list), Default filters, My views, Shared views, + New view, Manage views. A malformed condition is dropped one at a time and the rest of the view survives. An operator without the right sees a shared view but cannot edit or delete it. Not built: sharing to a single role, a keyboard-only way to pin from the dropdown (Alt+V then P still does it), more reports on the filter. Exercised in throw-away browser profiles, never under sync with a second device. BETA: built, reviewed, committed (c0d9aa3) and deployed 2026-10-20 (web app only), never used by a customer; checked in headless Chrome on macOS only. Not counted in the parity percentage.

beyond.name: Reports Center
beyond.note: One screen for every report: a catalogue of 99 reports in 14 categories (Business Overview, Sales, Receivables, Payables & Purchases, Inventory, Inventory Valuation, Banking, GST, TDS & TCS, Payroll & HR, Accountant, Cost Centres & Budgets, Activity & Audit, CRM), with counts that follow the company's feature switches and the operator's rights. Left panel: Home, Favourites, Recently visited, Shared reports, My reports, then the categories; the table has a star, name, category, created by and last visited, all sortable. Search is word-based and ranked like Go To, so 'udhaar', 'debtors', 'aging', 'invoices' and 'bs' each find their report. The star IS the left menu's pin (limit 8); last-visited is kept per company and operator. Opened from the Reports group, Gateway key O and Go To. Three rows (Ledger, Group Summary, Stock Item book) open a picker and cannot be starred. Not built: scheduled reports, advanced analytics. BETA: built, reviewed, committed (c0d9aa3) and deployed 2026-10-20 (web app only), never used by a customer; checked in headless Chrome on macOS only. Not counted in the parity percentage.

beyond.name: Create New Report
beyond.note: A short form (name, the report it is based on, category, personal or company-wide), then the real report with its F12 options, added columns and the row filter, under a Save / Cancel strip (Ctrl+A saves). beyond.name: Settings window: theme, accent, font, text size, workspace policy
beyond.note: A Settings window with three tabs, opened by Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on a Mac; it works inside a field), the top-bar gear, Go To, the Gateway Company menu (key Q) and the left menu's Preferences row. Appearance: theme Light / Dark / Same as my computer; one of eight accent colours (teal is today's, plus blue, indigo, violet, plum, berry, green, graphite; no free colour); a font (IBM Plex Sans, System font, Ledger in Plex Mono); text size 90 to 150 % by design tokens, not browser zoom; reduce motion; high contrast. Each applies at once, is kept per person on the device, and shows in a live preview. Workspace: the administrator sets company defaults and can lock the theme, accent, font, the standard button layouts and the menu's default view (text size, contrast and motion can be defaults but never locks, so a low-vision person keeps control), exports and imports the policy as JSON (a file with any invalid part is refused whole), resets it (asks first, No armed) and restores it when an older app version erased it. The policy is Company.ui, an optional synced field on the company row written by one function behind the write guard; with operator security on, only an operator with the Administration right can save it. A person who never opens Settings sees exactly the app as before: asserted by reference in the suites and by pixel on five screens, and printed paper never changes. The way back: Reset all my settings (asks first) and ?uireset=1 on the address. Every accent preset passes the full contrast matrix of visual.assert in both schemes; a 576-capture matrix (9 screens: the three Settings tabs and six others, x 8 accents x 2 schemes x 4 text sizes) found no console error, overflow, cut label or contrast failure, and it did find the Dashboard defect listed under Open. Server half: backend/src/conflict.js keeps the current Company.ui against a write from an older client that states no base revision; it was deployed 2026-10-23 with Phase 29's backend (the VM ran the a0fffd6 backend code until then) and has not been exercised on the VM; the client defence (revision, per-device mirror, Restore) still stands in front of it. No audited TallyPrime feature maps to this, so no parity row moved. BETA: built and reviewed (spec docs/design/settings-spec.md), committed (5c94342) and its web app deployed to the VM 2026-10-21 (the live URL was driven in headless Chrome: the st-fit-settings and st-look-settings-150 recipes passed with zero console errors; the backend half was deployed 2026-10-23, see above), never used by a customer; checked in headless Chrome on macOS only (real keys on Windows, Linux, Firefox, Safari and Electron are unchecked; Cmd+, in Safari and macOS Chrome is unverified). Open: at 150 % text size the Dashboard's Receivables and Payables card titles are drawn under the + New button (Dashboard v2 code exposed by the text size; 125 % and below are clean); 135 inline font sizes in rarely used screens stay unscaled; personal choices are per device (export and import to move them), with no synced per-user layer. Not counted in the parity percentage.

beyond.name: Configurable shortcuts, right-hand buttons and top bar
beyond.note: Settings > Shortcuts lets a person change keys without changing what any key means by default. A recorded key is ADDED as a second way to run an action (the original keeps working) unless the person turns the original off, row by row. 25 actions are rebindable (the F-keys on entry screens and statements, Alt+C, Alt+D, Alt+P, Alt+N, Alt+K, Alt+2, Alt+B and others) plus extra keys for Go To, the menu toggle, quick create and help. One translation layer at the keydown (src/keys.ts) turns the pressed key into the default chord, so no screen's key handler changed; the rail, the ? sheet, tooltips and the palette print the person's key. A swap (F8 and F9) works through the screen one step at a time, and a change that would silently drop both entries mid-swap is refused. Never rebindable: Esc, Enter, Tab, arrows, typing keys, Ctrl+A/Z/C/V/X/Y, Ctrl+K and Alt+G, Ctrl+\, Alt+Q, F1, Ctrl+, , the favourite slots, browser chords, and anything with Ctrl+Alt (AltGr) or Shift. The right-hand button rail and the top bar can hide, rename and reorder buttons, per person, with an administrator's company standard that can be locked: hiding a button never disables its key, Quit and Accept stay, and the top bar folds items under ... in a narrow window with the gear fixed. Export and import as JSON (refused whole when it is broken, names a reserved key, has an unknown field or hides Quit); Reset asks first. A hostile or garbage stored table is tested to leave F8, Ctrl+K, Enter, Esc and Ctrl+, working. With nothing stored the dispatcher hands every handler the same event object, and an empty layout returns the same array. No audited TallyPrime feature maps to this, so no parity row moved. BETA: built and reviewed, committed (5c94342) and its web app deployed to the VM 2026-10-21 (the live URL was driven in headless Chrome with the Settings recipes st-fit-settings and st-look-settings-150, zero console errors; the real-key flow settings-shortcuts-flow is not among the recipes reported against the live URL; an administrator's company standard layouts ride on Company.ui, whose server protection was deployed 2026-10-23, see b-settings), never used by a customer; checked in headless Chrome on macOS only (real presses on Windows, Linux, Firefox, Safari and Electron are unchecked; an Option+digit glyph on a real Mac keyboard is covered at event level only). Not built: the My buttons block (Favourite Shortcuts as extra rail buttons, off by default); layouts are global by button id, not per screen kind. 47 user-facing sentences still name a rebindable key by its standard name (held at a ceiling of 47). Not counted in the parity percentage.

beyond.name: Dashboard v2: period-aware board of charts, as-at figures and drill-through
beyond.note: The Dashboard is rebuilt as a board of 22 widgets drawn from a catalogue of 24 (Account watchlist and Highlights are catalogued with no implementation, so the board neither lists nor draws them). A header band carries a Period control (F2: six presets plus Custom), an As at switch (Today or Period end, kept per operator), Customize (F12) and the page's + New; every balance says the date it is as at. Charts are a small kit (columns, stacked bars, ranked bars, sparklines) whose series colours are validated by script in both schemes, with a tooltip, a 'View as table' twin that carries every figure, and keyboard access (one tab stop, Enter drills, Esc leaves). Every card opens the report it summarises on the same window, and each figure is reconciled to that report in the suites: Receivables and Payables to the debtor and creditor balances (an on-account receipt or an advance is shown as Unapplied, and a flipped balance prints Cr or Dr), Income and expense to the Profit and Loss with stock, Overdue to the Bills reports, Cash flow as opening + in - out = closing (a Contra between two banks is zero), Top expenses to Direct plus Indirect Expenses. Where a card cannot carry its date into the report it says what it left out (N vouchers are dated after today and left out here; the report counts them). Sales, Purchases and the trend open the Group Summary of the Sales or Purchase Accounts, because the register totals GST-inclusive values. The NEW DEFAULT board (for a person with no saved layout) is twelve widgets: Today, Get started, Receivables, Payables, Cash flow, Income and expense, Cash & Bank, Top expenses, Overdue invoices, GST payable, Recent Vouchers, Stock alerts; Quick Entry is off. A saved layout is never changed and widgets added later arrive off; a stored size a widget does not offer reads as its default. Edit mode (F12) has drag with a drop marker, an Add widgets gallery (search by label and by Tally or Zoho word, needs badges), keyboard moves (Space grabs, arrows move, Shift+Left/Right resize, H hides, S/M/L set the size, Esc cancels), per-widget settings (Top expenses: Top N, include purchases), Cancel changes, a 24-widget limit and a company layout that only an administrator can write. A widget the operator may not open is not drawn, not listed and not computed; a widget off the board is not computed; a Dashboard under another screen computes nothing; the Dashboard is still refused to Data Entry operators. A saved layout keeps every item field it does not know (the settings of a newer build survive a save by this one). Work runs in waves so the first paint carries the one-pass index (about 64 ms at 250,000 vouchers). Cost: with every widget on, engine time at 250,000 vouchers is about 718 ms against about 350 ms for the old default board (50,000: 125 against 64 ms), and the default board lists every pass; this is NOT gated, it is the GST payable tile building the open period (decision D8), and it was not measured as time to paint in a browser. Deliberately deferred: view widgets (a saved report as a widget) and the Overdue preset wait for the planned grid query core (core/listQuery.ts); the Overdue invoices list is a bespoke build marked REPLACE-WITH-LISTQUERY. Scheduled digests, anomaly alerts and share links are not built. Known difference: the Bills Receivable and Payable reports still decide a bill's side by sign alone while the card uses the ledger's group, so on a book with an advance on the other side the report can list a row the card calls unapplied. No audited TallyPrime feature maps to this, so no parity row moved. BETA: built and reviewed (design and contracts: docs/design/dashboard-v2-contracts.md), committed (5c94342, with Phase 27) and deployed to the VM 2026-10-21 (web app only, no backend change; the live URL was driven in headless Chrome: dash2-default, dash2-widgets-all, dash2-edit-board and dash2-period-menu passed with zero console errors), never used by a customer; checked in headless Chrome on macOS only (real touch input, a screen-reader pass, forced-colours rendering and real F-key and Ctrl presses on Windows, Linux, Firefox, Safari and Electron are unchecked). Open: at 150 % text size the Receivables and Payables card titles are drawn under the + New button (the card header rule is unchanged and no Dashboard v2 gate probed 150 %; 125 % and below are clean); Account watchlist and Highlights are not built. Not counted in the parity percentage.

beyond.name: AI connector (MCP server): a customer's own AI tool reads their books
beyond.note: A package (mcp/, @comhard/books-mcp 1.1.0, private, unpublished) and a backend plugin (backend/src/mcpRoute.js) that let a customer's own AI tool (Claude Desktop or Code, Cursor, VS Code and other MCP clients) read their books through an API key. 16 tools: 14 read (companies, find, receivables and payables, ledger statement, Trial Balance, Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet, cash and bank, sales and purchase analysis, stock, GST, TDS, voucher search, one voucher, data checks) and 2 draft-write (preview, then confirm, always saved as an Optional draft). Every figure comes from the app's own report engines, bundled read-only from src/core (52 files pinned by SHA-256); three data sources: the AI gateway, the plain REST API (small books) and a company backup file (offline). Read only by default; a key must be a read-scope key approved by an owner or administrator; draft ceilings of 25 open, 10 an hour, 50 a day and Rs 1 crore a day. THE PRODUCT STILL CALLS NO AI MODEL: this is an integration for the customer's own AI tool, and whatever a tool returns goes to that provider. Not a TallyPrime parity item and not counted in the parity percentage; do not market it as something TallyPrime lacks (community MCP servers for TallyPrime exist: docs/research/mcp-landscape.md). BUILT, NOT DEPLOYED: built and reviewed 2026-10-22 to 23 (a three-lens review round, mcp/CHANGELOG.md) and committed on main as d7846ce (not released). Gate 2026-10-23 (mcp's own, not the root gate): tsc 0, 41 core suites with 112,131 assertions, 15 remote-lane suites with 4,153, a real stdio smoke test with 112, 201 and 133 deliberate mutations all killed. The LOCAL half (stdio connector, backup file, REST API for small books) is BETA and unreleased: private package, never tried in a live AI client, only Node 25.2.1 run. The HOSTED half is IN DEVELOPMENT and cannot be switched on: no Postgres data layer (with MCP_ENABLED=1 the backend refuses to start), no compute worker, no write commit, not registered in backend/src/server.js, not on the VM, no TLS on the VM. Drafts cannot be saved on any server. claude.ai, Claude on a phone and ChatGPT are PLANNED (OAuth specified, not built). Open: the app-side AI-access screen and Edit Log mark, seam R5 (redactForRead returns a legacy vaultPin or pin to every read key) and seam K3, the .mcpb, npm publication and a licence, counsel on DPDP, an accountant on draft invoice number gaps. Out of step since 2026-10-25: 9 of the 52 engine files pinned in mcp/engine-lock.json changed in Phase 30 (1d22e84), so the drift guard fails until the package is re-reconciled and the lock re-recorded. See docs/HANDOFF.md section 2g, mcp/README.md and docs/design/mcp-server-spec.md.

beyond.name: Custom fields on masters, vouchers and item lines (v2)
beyond.note: Extends the live custom fields (b-udf: ledgers and stock items only). An administrator defines fields on ledgers, stock items, employees, leads, voucher headers (a strip under Narration) and item lines (up to two inline columns, the rest on a sub-row): 12 types (text, long text, number, amount, percent, date, yes/no, choice, multi-choice, email, phone, link) plus a lookup (a link to a ledger, item, employee or lead; masters only), with scope by voucher type and stock group, defaults, inheritance from the party or item, print switches, hide and a delete that keeps stored values, starter sets, a live preview, Fill blanks (one undo step) and custom columns in the mapped Excel/CSV importer and Bulk Entry. A mandatory field is enforced at every door per the company's entry rules (b-entry-rules); the cloud keeps the custom values an older app omits (capability udf2). BUILT, REVIEWED (five lenses with sceptic verification), FIXED and GATED in a worktree and merged into main as 1d22e84 on 2026-10-25; NOT DEPLOYED, BETA: the live site still has the v1 editor, no customer has used v2, and it was checked in headless Chrome on macOS only. A lookup is on masters only and cannot group; CSV Import Data and the legacy CSV importers have no custom column; Fill blanks covers voucher-header fields only. A no-code field is not TallyPrime's TDL: the parity row tdl-customization stays missing and this moves no parity row. See docs/HANDOFF.md section 2h, docs/design/custom-fields-spec.md and docs/design/cf-back-nav-build-notes.md.

beyond.name: Analysis by field: Summary, Income and expense, Bills, Balances and Stock by field
beyond.note: Five reports in a new last Reports Center group, Analysis by field (106 reports in 15 categories; reached from the Reports Center, Go To and the palette, with no left-rail or Gateway row): Summary by field, Income and expense by field (ties to the Profit and Loss nett), Bills by field and Balances by field (tie to the group balance) and Stock by field.
